How to Download Your Social Media Data

A step-by-step visual guide

Follow the numbered screenshots. Each picture shows exactly where to tap or click.

📸 Screen time 🎵 TikTok ▶️ YouTube ✅ Send
Before you start: Make sure you are logged in to your own account. When a format option appears, always choose JSON, which is the format this study can read. You do not need to share everything: On TikTok you can untick items (e.g. Direct Messages), and you will be able to review what you send before donating.

📸 Screen-time screenshots

take a few pictures of your usage stats
🤳 How to take a screenshot: iPhone: press Side button + Volume Up together. Android: press Power + Volume Down together. (Some phones use a different combo or a palm-swipe.)
📜 Please take more than one screenshot. The first screen usually does not show everything. Scroll all the way down and take several screenshots, so the chart, the totals, and the full app list (including anything hidden under a "Show more" link) are all captured.

📱 On iPhone

1
Open Screen Time

In Settings, scroll down and tap Screen Time.

2
See all activity

Tap See All App & Website Activity.

3
📸 Week view

On the Week tab, take a screenshot. It shows your daily average, categories and Total Screen Time.

4
📸 App list

Scroll to Most Used, tap Show More, and screenshot the list. It shows TikTok, YouTube and the rest with their times.

5
📸 Day view

Tap the Day tab and screenshot that too.

🤖 On Android

📸 Digital Wellbeing

Open Settings → Digital Wellbeing & parental controls. Screenshot the chart, then scroll to the app list at the bottom (TikTok, YouTube…).
Illustration. Your screen may look a little different on Samsung, Xiaomi, Pixel, etc.

TikTok

On the TikTok phone app
1
Settings and privacy

Go to your Profile, tap the ☰ menu, then tap Settings and privacy.

2
Account

Tap Account.

3
Download your data

Tap Download your data.

4
Choose JSON

Under File format, choose JSON (not TXT), the format the study needs.

5
Tick data & Request

Under Select data to download, tap Select all (or tick the items you agree to share, and you may leave Direct Messages unticked). Then tap Request data.

6
Download

Open the Download data tab. When your file is ready, tap Download (available for 4 days).

YouTube

In a web browser at takeout.google.com
1
Select YouTube only

Go to takeout.google.com. Click Deselect all, then scroll down and tick only YouTube and YouTube Music. Click Next step.

2
Create export

Set Transfer to = Send download link via email, Frequency = Export once, File type = .zip. Click Create export.

3
Open the email

Wait for Google's email “Your Google data is ready to download”, then click Manage Google Takeout request.

4
Download

On the export page, click Download and save the ZIP file.

✅ Final step: clean & upload at your visit

your data stays private
  1. Before your visit, clean your data. 🧹 Open the Data Donation Cleaner This opens the cleaner in your web browser. It works on your phone or a computer, and there is nothing to install. Tap Choose your ZIP file and pick the ZIP you downloaded from TikTok or YouTube. The cleaner keeps only what the study needs and removes personal content. It all happens on your own device, and nothing is sent anywhere. Tap Create my cleaned file and it saves a clean file to your Downloads. Do this once for TikTok and once for YouTube.
  2. Bring your phone to your visit. Make sure it has your cleaned file(s) and your screen-time screenshots on it.
  3. At the visit, scan the QR code to upload. When you finish the questionnaire on the lab computer, it will show a QR code. Scan it with your phone’s camera. It opens a secure upload page where you add your cleaned file(s) and your screen-time screenshots. Please upload the cleaned files, not the original ZIPs.
  4. It is secure. Your files go only to Qualtrics, the University of Leeds’ approved survey platform, and are linked to your participant number, not your name. If anything does not work, the researcher will help you at the visit.

Approved by the University of Leeds School ethics committee · Ref SoPREC 4202. Any questions, contact the research team.

Platform menus change from time to time, so a button may sit in a slightly different place than these steps. If you get stuck at any point, contact the research team.
